class.name: Camera3D
class.brief_description: Camera node, displays from a point of view.
class.description: [Camera3D] is a special node that displays what is visible from its current location. Cameras register themselves in the nearest [Viewport] node (when ascending the tree). Only one camera can be active per viewport. If no viewport is available ascending the tree, the camera will register in the global viewport. In other words, a camera just provides 3D display capabilities to a [Viewport], and, without one, a scene registered in that [Viewport] (or higher viewports) can't be displayed.

method.name: autofocus_trigger
method.description: Starts a single autofocus (like half-pressing a shutter button) when [member autofocus_mode] is [constant AUTOFOCUS_MODE_SINGLE]: measures the distance once, from [member autofocus_target] or [member autofocus_points], and drives the lens there. Emits [signal focus_acquired] when focus is reached, or [signal focus_failed] right away if nothing was measured. Does nothing in the other modes.

method.name: clear_current
method.description: If this is the current camera, remove it from being current. If [param enable_next] is [code]true[/code], request to make the next camera current, if any.

method.name: get_autofocus_distance
method.description: Returns the distance in meters the autofocus lens is currently focused at, which may differ from the measured subject distance while the lens is moving.

method.name: get_camera_projection
method.description: Returns the projection matrix that this camera uses to render to its associated viewport. The camera must be part of the scene tree to function.

method.name: get_camera_rid
method.description: Returns the camera's RID from the [RenderingServer].

method.name: get_camera_transform
method.description: Returns the transform of the camera plus the vertical ([member v_offset]) and horizontal ([member h_offset]) offsets; and any other adjustments made to the position and orientation of the camera by subclassed cameras such as [XRCamera3D].

method.name: get_cull_mask_value
method.description: Returns whether or not the specified layer of the [member cull_mask] is enabled, given a [param layer_number] between 1 and 20.

method.name: get_frustum
method.description: Returns the camera's frustum planes in world space units as an array of [Plane]s in the following order: near, far, left, top, right, bottom. Not to be confused with [member frustum_offset].

method.name: get_monitoring_clean_texture
method.description: Returns the camera's image without its monitoring overlays while [member monitoring_clean_texture_enabled] is [code]true[/code], or [code]null[/code] otherwise. It is the same [Texture2D] for as long as the property stays enabled; read it with [method Texture2D.get_image_async], or draw it like any other texture (in a [TextureRect], for example). [codeblock] # "Download Image": the photo without the zebras or false color the monitor shows. func save_photo(): $Camera3D.monitoring_clean_texture_enabled = true $Camera3D.get_monitoring_clean_texture().get_image_async(func(image: Image): $Camera3D.monitoring_clean_texture_enabled = false if image: image.save_png("user://photo.png")) [/codeblock] Or, with [code]await[/code] ([code]Texture2D.get_image_awaitable()[/code] returns a signal that fires once with the [Image] or [code]null[/code]): [codeblock] func save_photo(): $Camera3D.monitoring_clean_texture_enabled = true var image: Image = await $Camera3D.get_monitoring_clean_texture().get_image_awaitable() $Camera3D.monitoring_clean_texture_enabled = false if image: image.save_png("user://photo.png") [/codeblock] The read is of the frame drawn at the end of the current frame, so enabling the property and reading the texture in the same function works. The image has the size and format of the viewport's own texture ([method Viewport.get_texture]).

method.name: get_monitoring_histogram
method.description:
Returns the latest histogram read back from the GPU for [param channel]: 256 pixel counts, one per 8-bit code value (bin [code]i[/code] counts the pixels whose value rounds to [code]i / 255[/code]). Returns an empty array while [member monitoring_histogram_enabled] is [code]false[/code], and until the first readback arrives. The counts are of the display-encoded image (nonlinear, as it is shown), after tonemapping and [CameraAttributes]' noise reduction and sharpening, and before the monitoring overlays (zebras, false color, focus peaking, the histogram itself), so turning those on or off does not change them. Luma is Rec. 709 Y' of the display-encoded values. Each channel's counts add up to the width times the height of the viewport's 3D render target, so [code]count / (width * height)[/code] is a fraction of the frame. The first call starts the readback, as does connecting to [signal monitoring_histogram_updated]; it then runs while the histogram is enabled, independently of [member monitoring_visible_in_output] and [member monitoring_histogram_draw]. The readback is asynchronous and never stalls rendering: the result is one or more frames old, and on the web the first frames return an empty array. [member monitoring_histogram_update_interval] throttles it. Each camera has its own histogram, so two cameras rendering in the same frame each return their own; a camera rendered into several viewports returns the latest of them. [codeblock] func _ready(): $Camera3D.monitoring_histogram_enabled = true $Camera3D.monitoring_histogram_draw = false # The app draws its own. $Camera3D.monitoring_histogram_update_interval = 0.25 $Camera3D.monitoring_histogram_updated.connect(_on_histogram)
func _on_histogram(): var luma = $Camera3D.get_monitoring_histogram() var highlights_clipping = false for i in range(250, 256): highlights_clipping = highlights_clipping or luma[i] > 0 [/codeblock] [b]Note:[/b] Only supported in the Forward+ and Mobile rendering methods. In Compatibility, which has no compute shaders, it always returns an empty array. Not available in XR (multiview) rendering.

method.name: get_pyramid_shape_rid
method.description: Returns the RID of a pyramid shape encompassing the camera's view frustum, ignoring the camera's near plane. The tip of the pyramid represents the position of the camera.

method.name: get_shake_offset
method.description: Returns the handheld shake offset applied this frame, in the camera's own frame of reference (identity when [member shake_enabled] is [code]false[/code]). The rendered camera transform, also returned by [method get_camera_transform], is the node's global transform multiplied by this offset; the node's own [member Node3D.transform] never includes it.

method.name: is_autofocus_acquired
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the autofocus has reached its subject (see [signal focus_acquired]).

method.name: is_position_behind
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the given position is behind the camera (the blue part of the linked diagram). [url=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/godotengine/godot-docs/master/img/camera3d_position_frustum.png]See this diagram[/url] for an overview of position query methods. [b]Note:[/b] A position which returns [code]false[/code] may still be outside the camera's field of view.

method.name: is_position_in_frustum
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the given position is inside the camera's frustum (the green part of the linked diagram). [url=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/godotengine/godot-docs/master/img/camera3d_position_frustum.png]See this diagram[/url] for an overview of position query methods.

method.name: make_current
method.description: Makes this camera the current camera for the [Viewport] (see class description). If the camera node is outside the scene tree, it will attempt to become current once it's added.

method.name: project_local_ray_normal
method.description: Returns a normal vector from the screen point location directed along the camera. Orthogonal cameras are normalized. Perspective cameras account for perspective, screen width/height, etc. [b]Note:[/b] Follows the Panini projection of the camera attributes in effect ([member CameraAttributes.panini_enabled]), so the result matches the image the camera shows.

method.name: project_position
method.description: Returns the 3D point in world space that maps to the given 2D coordinate in the [Viewport] rectangle on a plane that is the given [param z_depth] distance into the scene away from the camera. [b]Note:[/b] Follows the Panini projection of the camera attributes in effect ([member CameraAttributes.panini_enabled]), so the result matches the image the camera shows.

method.name: project_ray_normal
method.description: Returns a normal vector in world space, that is the result of projecting a point on the [Viewport] rectangle by the inverse camera projection. This is useful for casting rays in the form of (origin, normal) for object intersection or picking. [b]Note:[/b] Follows the Panini projection of the camera attributes in effect ([member CameraAttributes.panini_enabled]), so the result matches the image the camera shows.

method.name: project_ray_origin
method.description: Returns a 3D position in world space, that is the result of projecting a point on the [Viewport] rectangle by the inverse camera projection. This is useful for casting rays in the form of (origin, normal) for object intersection or picking.

method.name: set_cull_mask_value
method.description: Based on [param value], enables or disables the specified layer in the [member cull_mask], given a [param layer_number] between 1 and 20.

method.name: set_frustum
method.description: Sets the camera projection to frustum mode (see [constant PROJECTION_FRUSTUM]), by specifying a [param size], an [param offset], and the [param z_near] and [param z_far] clip planes in world space units. The [param size] parameter represents the size of the near plane, either its width or height depending on the value of [member keep_aspect]. See also [member frustum_offset].

method.name: set_orthogonal
method.description: Sets the camera projection to orthogonal mode (see [constant PROJECTION_ORTHOGONAL]), by specifying a [param size], and the [param z_near] and [param z_far] clip planes in world space units. As a hint, 3D games that look 2D often use this projection, with [param size] specified in pixels.

method.name: set_perspective
method.description: Sets the camera projection to perspective mode (see [constant PROJECTION_PERSPECTIVE]), by specifying a [param fov] (field of view) angle in degrees, and the [param z_near] and [param z_far] clip planes in world space units.

method.name: unproject_position
method.description: Returns the 2D coordinate in the [Viewport] rectangle that maps to the given 3D point in world space. [b]Note:[/b] Follows the Panini projection of the camera attributes in effect ([member CameraAttributes.panini_enabled]), so the result matches the image the camera shows. [b]Note:[/b] When using this to position GUI elements over a 3D viewport, use [method is_position_behind] to prevent them from appearing if the 3D point is behind the camera: [codeblock] # This code block is part of a script that inherits from Node3D. # `control` is a reference to a node inheriting from Control. control.visible = not get_viewport().get_camera_3d().is_position_behind(global_transform.origin) control.position = get_viewport().get_camera_3d().unproject_position(global_transform.origin) [/codeblock]

members.member: The [CameraAttributes] to use for this camera.
The physics layers the autofocus rays of [member autofocus_points] can hit. Use it to keep glass, triggers or the player's own body from taking focus.

The fraction by which the lens overshoots its target before settling, the back-and-forth "hunting" of contrast-detect autofocus. [code]0.0[/code] approaches the target smoothly without overshoot, as phase-detect autofocus does. The envelope of the motion still decays with [member autofocus_time_constant].

How the camera focuses. In [constant AUTOFOCUS_MODE_SINGLE] and [constant AUTOFOCUS_MODE_CONTINUOUS] the camera drives the focus of its [member attributes]: [member CameraAttributesPhysical.frustum_focus_distance], or for [CameraAttributesPractical] the near and far blur distances and transitions, which are moved together around the focus distance keeping the width of the in-focus band constant in diopters (1 / distance), as a real lens's depth of field does. With only far blur enabled, the in-focus band is taken to be centered at half the far distance; with only near blur, the far limit is at infinity. Autofocus runs in the editor too, so the camera preview shows the result. Saving the scene stores the values you set, not the ones autofocus wrote; editing them while autofocus runs makes them the new starting point. Switching back to [constant AUTOFOCUS_MODE_MANUAL] leaves the focus where autofocus put it. [b]Note:[/b] Autofocus writes to the attributes resource. A resource shared by several cameras is focused by all of them; give each autofocusing camera its own resource (for example with [member Resource.resource_local_to_scene]). [b]Note:[/b] Ray-cast measurement ([member autofocus_points]) uses the direct space state from the main thread, so it does not work with [member ProjectSettings.physics/3d/run_on_separate_thread] enabled; [member autofocus_target] works in all cases.

Normalized screen points (0 to 1, [code]Vector2(0.5, 0.5)[/code] is the center, Y down) where autofocus measures distance with a physics ray cast, like a phase-detect or laser rangefinder sensor. With several points, the nearest hit wins (closest-subject priority of zone autofocus). Used when [member autofocus_target] is empty or does not point to a [Node3D].
A [Node3D] the autofocus tracks: its distance along the camera's optical axis is the focus distance. Takes priority over [member autofocus_points].

How fast the focus moves, in seconds: the remaining focus error, measured in diopters (1 / distance), falls by a factor of [code]e[/code] (to 37%) every time constant, so focus is 95% of the way after three time constants whatever the frame rate. A focus motor's travel is close to linear in diopters, which is why a focus change from 1 m to 2 m takes as long as one from 2 m to infinity.
The [Compositor] to use for this camera.

The culling mask that describes which [member VisualInstance3D.layers] are rendered by this camera. By default, all 20 user-visible layers are rendered. [b]Note:[/b] Since the [member cull_mask] allows for 32 layers to be stored in total, there are an additional 12 layers that are only used internally by the engine and aren't exposed in the editor. Setting [member cull_mask] using a script allows you to toggle those reserved layers, which can be useful for editor plugins. To adjust [member cull_mask] more easily using a script, use [method get_cull_mask_value] and [method set_cull_mask_value]. [b]Note:[/b] [VoxelGI], SDFGI and [LightmapGI] will always take all layers into account to determine what contributes to global illumination. If this is an issue, set [member GeometryInstance3D.gi_mode] to [constant GeometryInstance3D.GI_MODE_DISABLED] for meshes and [member Light3D.light_bake_mode] to [constant Light3D.BAKE_DISABLED] for lights to exclude them from global illumination.

If [code]true[/code], the ancestor [Viewport] is currently using this camera. If multiple cameras are in the scene, one will always be made current. For example, if two [Camera3D] nodes are present in the scene and only one is current, setting one camera's [member current] to [code]false[/code] will cause the other camera to be made current.

If not [constant DOPPLER_TRACKING_DISABLED], this camera will simulate the [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doppler_effect]Doppler effect[/url] for objects changed in particular [code]_process[/code] methods. [b]Note:[/b] The Doppler effect will only be heard on [AudioStreamPlayer3D]s if [member AudioStreamPlayer3D.doppler_tracking] is not set to [constant AudioStreamPlayer3D.DOPPLER_TRACKING_DISABLED].
The [Environment] to use for this camera.

The distance to the far culling boundary for this camera relative to its local Z axis. Higher values allow the camera to see further away, while decreasing [member far] can improve performance if it results in objects being partially or fully culled.

The camera's field of view (also known as FOV), as an angle in degrees. Only applicable in perspective mode. Since [member keep_aspect] locks one axis, this property sets the field of view on the other axis. For reference, the default angle for the vertical FOV ([code]75.0[/code]) is equivalent to a horizontal FOV of: - ~91.31 degrees in a 4:3 viewport - ~101.67 degrees in a 16:10 viewport - ~107.51 degrees in a 16:9 viewport - ~121.63 degrees in a 21:9 viewport

The camera's frustum offset. This can be changed from the default to create "tilted frustum" effects such as [url=https://zdoom.org/wiki/Y-shearing]Y-shearing[/url]. [b]Note:[/b] Only effective if [member projection] is [constant PROJECTION_FRUSTUM].
The horizontal (X) offset of the camera viewport.
The axis to lock during [member fov]/[member size] adjustments. Can be either [constant KEEP_WIDTH] or [constant KEEP_HEIGHT].

If [code]true[/code], every frame this camera renders is also copied, without its monitoring overlays, into the texture [method get_monitoring_clean_texture] returns: the 3D image after tonemapping and [CameraAttributes]' noise reduction and sharpening, before the zebras, false color, focus peaking and drawn histogram, and before any 2D drawn over the viewport. It is what the viewport's own texture would show with the overlays off, so a script can save or show the picture the camera records while its monitor shows the overlays, without rendering the scene a second time. This costs one texture the size of the viewport and one copy per rendered frame while enabled, whether or not any overlay is on, and nothing while disabled: disabling it frees the texture (a script that kept the [Texture2D] then reads [code]null[/code] from it). Enable it only while needed, as in the example in [method get_monitoring_clean_texture]. It works in the running project whatever [member monitoring_visible_in_output] says (without the overlays, the copy is simply the image). Each camera has its own texture, so two viewports with their own cameras each keep their own. A camera rendered into several viewports keeps the latest one's. Until the camera has rendered a frame (for example, its [SubViewport]'s [member SubViewport.render_target_update_mode] is [constant SubViewport.UPDATE_DISABLED]), the texture is a placeholder, and later it keeps the last frame rendered. [b]Note:[/b] Supported in every rendering method, including Compatibility and the web. Not in XR (multiview) rendering.

If [code]true[/code], the image is replaced by an exposure map using the ARRI ALEXA false color bands on the video level (IRE): purple below 2.5 (black clipping), blue from 2.5 to 4, green from 38 to 42 (18% middle gray), pink from 52 to 56 (one stop over middle gray, typical light skin), yellow from 97 to 99 and red from 99 (white clipping). Everything else is shown in gray at its own luma. This overlay follows [member monitoring_visible_in_output].
The color [member monitoring_focus_peaking_enabled] paints in-focus edges with.

If [code]true[/code], edges that are in focus are painted in [member monitoring_focus_peaking_color]. Edges are found from the gradient of the display image's luma (a Sobel operator): detail in focus has steep gradients, and defocus (depth of field) spreads them out. Low-contrast surfaces show no peaking even when in focus, as on a camera. This overlay follows [member monitoring_visible_in_output].

How weak an edge still counts as in focus for [member monitoring_focus_peaking_enabled], from [code]0.0[/code] (only the strongest edges, a luma step of 40% within a pixel) to [code]1.0[/code] (edges of 3%).

If [code]true[/code], [member monitoring_histogram_enabled] draws the histogram over the image (following [member monitoring_visible_in_output]). If [code]false[/code], nothing is drawn and the histogram is only counted for [method get_monitoring_histogram], on the frames a readback is due: for a project that shows the histogram in its own UI.

If [code]true[/code], a histogram of the frame (256 bins, one per 8-bit code value of the display image) is counted on the GPU every frame and drawn in a corner of the image, its bars scaled to the tallest bin. This overlay follows [member monitoring_visible_in_output]. Scripts can read the counts with [method get_monitoring_histogram]; [member monitoring_histogram_draw] turns the drawing off. [b]Note:[/b] Only supported in the Forward+ and Mobile rendering methods, which have compute shaders, not Compatibility.
Whether [member monitoring_histogram_enabled] shows the luma histogram or the red, green and blue ones overlaid.
The opacity of the histogram over the image.
The corner of the image [member monitoring_histogram_enabled] draws the histogram in. It is inset from the corner by 3% of the image height.
The width of the histogram as a fraction of the image width. Its height is half its width.

The time in seconds between two readbacks of the histogram for [method get_monitoring_histogram] and [signal monitoring_histogram_updated]. [code]0.0[/code] reads it back every frame. A UI that redraws a few times a second can use [code]0.25[/code], which also saves the counting on the frames in between when [member monitoring_histogram_draw] is [code]false[/code].

If [code]false[/code], the monitoring overlays ([member monitoring_zebras_enabled], [member monitoring_focus_peaking_enabled], [member monitoring_false_color_enabled], [member monitoring_histogram_enabled]) are only drawn in the editor, where the editor renders through this camera: the 3D viewport's camera preview and the Camera3D inspector preview. A running project then draws none of them and does no work for them. If [code]true[/code], they are also drawn in the running project. The overlays are drawn over the finished 3D image, after tonemapping and [CameraAttributes]' noise reduction and sharpening, and under any 2D drawn on top of the viewport. [b]Note:[/b] The overlays are only drawn for single-view rendering, not in XR.

The color of the stripes [member monitoring_zebras_enabled] draws, as a display (sRGB-encoded) color, like [member monitoring_focus_peaking_color]. Defaults to black, which shows on the bright areas this zebra marks.

If [code]true[/code], diagonal stripes ([member monitoring_zebras_color], black by default), crawling as on a camera's monitor, are drawn over the parts of the image whose video level is at or above [member monitoring_zebras_level]. The video level is the Rec. 709 luma of the display-encoded image, in IRE (percent of full range). This overlay follows [member monitoring_visible_in_output].
The video level, in IRE (percent of full-range Rec. 709 luma), at and above which [member monitoring_zebras_enabled] draws its stripes. The default of 95 marks highlights about to clip.
The color of the stripes [member monitoring_zebras_second_enabled] draws, as a display (sRGB-encoded) color. Defaults to white. Where both zebras mark a pixel, [member monitoring_zebras_color] wins.

If [code]true[/code], a second zebra of stripes ([member monitoring_zebras_second_color], white by default), running the other way, is drawn over the parts of the image within ±5 IRE of [member monitoring_zebras_second_level], the window cameras offer for judging skin exposure. This overlay follows [member monitoring_visible_in_output].
The center, in IRE, of the ±5 IRE window [member monitoring_zebras_second_enabled] marks. The default of 70 is a common skin-tone exposure target.

The distance to the near culling boundary for this camera relative to its local Z axis. Lower values allow the camera to see objects more up close to its origin, at the cost of lower precision across the [i]entire[/i] range. Values lower than the default can lead to increased Z-fighting.
The camera's projection mode. In [constant PROJECTION_PERSPECTIVE] mode, objects' Z distance from the camera's local space scales their perceived size.
RMS amplitude of the slow pitch sway from the operator's breathing, in degrees.
Frequency of the breathing sway, in hertz. People at rest breathe 12 to 20 times a minute (0.2 to 0.33 Hz).

If [code]true[/code], the camera moves as if held by hand: procedural rotation and position noise, plus breathing sway, applied as an offset on top of the node's transform. The node's own [member Node3D.transform] and [member Node3D.global_transform] are not changed, so gameplay code keeps working; [method get_camera_transform] and the projection methods such as [method project_ray_normal] include the offset, so picking matches what is rendered. The motion is deterministic for a given [member shake_seed] and frame times, and in the editor it moves the camera preview only with [member shake_visible_in_editor] on. [member shake_preset] fills in every shake setting for a typical way of holding or mounting a camera.
RMS amplitude of the position shake along the camera's local X, Y and Z axes, in meters.
Center frequency of the position shake per local axis, in hertz. Each axis's motion is band-limited noise spread over two octaves around it (half to twice the frequency).

Fills in every shake setting ([member shake_rotation_amplitude], [member shake_rotation_frequency], [member shake_position_amplitude], [member shake_position_frequency], [member shake_breathing_amplitude], [member shake_breathing_frequency], [member shake_stabilization] and [member shake_scale_with_focal_length]) for a typical way of holding or mounting a camera; [member shake_seed] and [member shake_enabled] are left alone. Changing any of those settings afterwards switches this back to [constant SHAKE_PRESET_CUSTOM], keeping the values. Choosing [constant SHAKE_PRESET_CUSTOM] changes nothing. The values each preset writes are listed with its constant. They are drawn from measurements where they exist (the CIPA DC-X011 hand-shake band of about 1-10 Hz, postural sway, walking and running step frequencies, vehicle ride frequencies); the sources are cited in the engine's source code.
RMS amplitude of the rotation shake around the camera's local X (pitch), Y (yaw) and Z (roll) axes, in degrees.

Center frequency of the rotation shake per axis, in hertz. Each axis's motion is band-limited noise spread over two octaves around it (half to twice the frequency). Hand and arm sway concentrate below about 5 Hz; the defaults are a camera held in two hands while standing.

If [code]true[/code], the rotation amplitudes are angles, so a longer lens (smaller [member fov]) shows more shake in the frame, as with a real camera. If [code]false[/code], the amplitudes are as seen through a 50 mm lens on a full-frame sensor (a vertical field of view of 27 degrees) and scale with [member fov], so the shake keeps its size on screen while zooming. Position shake is not affected.
Seed of the shake noise. Cameras with the same seed and settings shake identically.

Strength of the image stabilization, from [code]0.0[/code] (none) to [code]1.0[/code]. Like optical or sensor-shift stabilization, it removes that fraction of the shake above about 0.5 Hz (the high-pass cutoff stabilizers use so as not to fight intentional pans) and progressively less below it, so slow breathing sway mostly remains.

If [code]true[/code], the shake also moves this camera in the editor (the 3D viewport's camera preview and the Camera3D inspector preview). If [code]false[/code] (the default), the camera holds still in the editor so shots can be framed, and does no shake work there. A running project always shakes while [member shake_enabled] is on; this setting has no effect there. Autofocus is unaffected and always runs in the editor.
The camera's size in meters measured as the diameter of the width or height, depending on [member keep_aspect]. Only applicable in orthogonal and frustum modes.
The vertical (Y) offset of the camera viewport.

signal.name: focus_acquired
signal.description: Emitted when the autofocus reaches its subject: the focus error is within a quarter of the depth of field (computed from the aperture and focal length of [CameraAttributesPhysical], or from the in-focus band of [CameraAttributesPractical]). [param distance] is the lens's focus distance in meters at that moment. In continuous mode, it is emitted again after focus was lost and reached anew.

signal.name: focus_failed
signal.description: Emitted when the autofocus finds nothing to focus on: [method autofocus_trigger] measured nothing, or continuous autofocus lost its subject. The focus stays where it was.

signal.name: monitoring_histogram_updated
signal.description: Emitted when a new histogram readback has arrived, so [method get_monitoring_histogram] returns new counts: at most once per frame, and about once per [member monitoring_histogram_update_interval]. Connecting to it starts the readback while [member monitoring_histogram_enabled] is [code]true[/code].

constants.constant: Perspective projection. Objects on the screen becomes smaller when they are far away.
Orthogonal projection, also known as orthographic projection. Objects remain the same size on the screen no matter how far away they are.
Frustum projection. This mode allows adjusting [member frustum_offset] to create "tilted frustum" effects.

Preserves the horizontal aspect ratio; also known as Vert- scaling. This is usually the best option for projects running in portrait mode, as taller aspect ratios will benefit from a wider vertical FOV.

Preserves the vertical aspect ratio; also known as Hor+ scaling. This is usually the best option for projects running in landscape mode, as wider aspect ratios will automatically benefit from a wider horizontal FOV.
Disables [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doppler_effect]Doppler effect[/url] simulation (default).

Simulate [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doppler_effect]Doppler effect[/url] by tracking positions of objects that are changed in [code]_process[/code]. Changes in the relative velocity of this camera compared to those objects affect how audio is perceived (changing the audio's [member AudioStreamPlayer3D.pitch_scale]).

Simulate [url=https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doppler_effect]Doppler effect[/url] by tracking positions of objects that are changed in [code]_physics_process[/code]. Changes in the relative velocity of this camera compared to those objects affect how audio is perceived (changing the audio's [member AudioStreamPlayer3D.pitch_scale]).
Autofocus is off; the focus is whatever the [member attributes] say.
Single autofocus (AF-S): focuses once each time [method autofocus_trigger] is called, then holds that focus.
Continuous autofocus (AF-C): measures every frame and keeps the subject in focus.
Hand-tuned values: choosing it changes nothing. A camera starts here, with the default values.

Holding the camera still, as for a photograph: hand shake in the 1.5-6 Hz band (CIPA DC-X011), slow postural sway and resting breath. Rotation [code]Vector3(0.12, 0.12, 0.06)[/code] degrees at [code]Vector3(3, 3, 2.5)[/code] Hz, position [code]Vector3(0.001, 0.001, 0.0005)[/code] m at 0.5 Hz, breathing 0.1 degrees at 0.25 Hz, no stabilization. [member shake_scale_with_focal_length] on.

[constant SHAKE_PRESET_HANDHELD] with a lens or sensor-shift stabilizer: the same values with [member shake_stabilization] at 0.8, which reduces the hand-shake band to about a fifth. [member shake_scale_with_focal_length] on.

Walking with the camera in hand: pitch and vertical bob at the step frequency (2 Hz), yaw, roll and sideways sway at the stride frequency (1 Hz). Rotation [code]Vector3(0.8, 0.6, 0.5)[/code] degrees at [code]Vector3(2, 1, 1)[/code] Hz, position [code]Vector3(0.008, 0.012, 0.005)[/code] m at [code]Vector3(1, 2, 2)[/code] Hz, breathing 0.15 degrees at 0.4 Hz. [member shake_scale_with_focal_length] on.

Running or action: the walking pattern at a running step frequency (2.8 Hz) and larger. Rotation [code]Vector3(2, 1.5, 1.5)[/code] degrees at [code]Vector3(2.8, 1.4, 1.4)[/code] Hz, position [code]Vector3(0.015, 0.03, 0.01)[/code] m at [code]Vector3(1.4, 2.8, 2.8)[/code] Hz, breathing 0.3 degrees at 0.7 Hz. [member shake_scale_with_focal_length] on.

A shoulder-mounted camera: slower body sway instead of hand shake. Rotation [code]Vector3(0.15, 0.2, 0.2)[/code] degrees at [code]Vector3(1.2, 1, 0.8)[/code] Hz, position [code]Vector3(0.003, 0.003, 0.002)[/code] m at 0.8 Hz, breathing 0.12 degrees at 0.25 Hz. [member shake_scale_with_focal_length] on.

A gimbal or stabilizer while walking: almost no rotation (a slow residual drift), while the walking bob, which a gimbal does not remove, passes through damped. Rotation [code]Vector3(0.03, 0.03, 0.02)[/code] degrees at 0.5 Hz, position [code]Vector3(0.004, 0.006, 0.003)[/code] m at [code]Vector3(1, 2, 2)[/code] Hz, no breathing. [member shake_scale_with_focal_length] on.

A tripod in a light wind: no operator, a small vibration at the tripod's resonance. Rotation [code]Vector3(0.03, 0.03, 0.01)[/code] degrees and position [code]Vector3(0.0002, 0.0002, 0.0001)[/code] m, both at 10 Hz, no breathing. Most visible on long lenses. [member shake_scale_with_focal_length] on.

A camera hard-mounted on a car: body bounce, pitch and roll at the suspension's ride frequency (1-1.2 Hz) and a yaw buzz from the wheels (8 Hz). Rotation [code]Vector3(0.3, 0.1, 0.3)[/code] degrees at [code]Vector3(1.2, 8, 1)[/code] Hz, position [code]Vector3(0.003, 0.01, 0.003)[/code] m at [code]Vector3(1, 1.2, 1.2)[/code] Hz, no breathing. [member shake_scale_with_focal_length] on.
